name: OR-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 6-point Democratic partisan lean in a favorable environment
Incumbent Val Hoyle's fundraising advantage ($1.2M raised vs. $0.7M for DeSpain)
Prediction markets price Hoyle near 95% to win
No public general-election polling to refine the estimate
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Hoyle: a D+6 seat, incumbency, and a clear money edge, with markets pricing her around 95%. DeSpain has raised enough to run a credible race, but nothing in the evidence suggests a shift large enough to threaten the seat.
model.watch: Any late polling showing DeSpain within single digits, or a surge of outside spending against Hoyle, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Val Hoyle seeks a second term in a southwestern Oregon district that leans Democratic by about six points. She holds a clear financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.2 million to Monique DeSpain's $0.7 million, and enters with the benefits of incumbency in a year when the national environment also favors her party. Prediction markets put her chances near 95 percent.

DeSpain, a first-time candidate, has modest resources and no outside spending recorded on either side so far. No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing. The race remains Safe Democratic, with some room for uncertainty given the absence of polling.
